procedure_signature.notes: Cable tension modelling — the cable force has a known line of action along the cable and a known pulling sense, leaving only the magnitude unknown, which is what makes a cable simpler than a general support. All three defining properties are authored: tension-only pulling away from each body, one magnitude throughout an ideal cable, and a frictionless pulley that changes direction but not magnitude, with the slack rule that a required compression sends the tension to zero. The pulling sense is stated per body — upward and away on the weight, toward the pulley and away on the hand. THE MODELLING READ HELD THE CRITICAL LINE: T = W is established as a direct read of a single weight on a single vertical cable segment, explicitly without writing or solving an equilibrium equation system, so the skill fixes the tension relation the geometry forces and hands the equilibrium solve to the equilibrium skills. The inclined segment carries the same T = W and the hand pulls with magnitude W regardless of the incline angle, the angle changing direction not magnitude. LATERAL BOUNDARIES against two signed siblings in the same subtopic are drawn in one sentence each and identify the basis of difference rather than a surface fact: support_reaction_modeling covers reactions that may push and may have unknown direction, against a cable that only pulls with geometry-fixed direction; contact_force_modeling covers a normal force that pushes perpendicular to a surface, against a cable that pulls along its length — opposite in sense and different in direction basis. Neither is re-authored. particle_fbd_2d owns the diagram and none is drawn; force_directed_along_line owns resolving a KNOWN magnitude into Cartesian components and is handed that work, the reciprocal being correct since that skill takes the magnitude as known while this one leaves it unknown; no equilibrium is solved as the deliverable; the pulley is ideal and frictionless with belt friction excluded as a different subject. The consistency check verifies that one shared T, two distinct directions, a pulling sense at each end, and a non-negative magnitude cohere — exactly what a frictionless pulley produces — and rejects a model assigning unequal magnitudes across the pulley. Two earned signals at distinct steps: sign_or_placement_error at step 2 where the cable force sense is assigned and drawing it as a push is the failure, and unclassified at step 1 as the boundary fallback. axis_confusion, simple_average_used and solution_sequencing_error cannot be earned: no axis chosen or transformed, not a Centroids-family skill, and the property statements are independent with no stranded prerequisite chain. Symbol reuse minimal and deliberate: T and W reused from particle_fbd_2d with identical meaning, and the incline is described in prose with no angle symbol bound, sidestepping the theta collision rather than managing it. Honest limitation recorded: the consistency check confirms the representation is internally coherent — one magnitude, fixed directions, pulling sense — but does not determine the numerical value of T from the wider problem, which requires equilibrium of the supported body, and a model can be internally consistent while the assumed geometry is wrong. This draft required no correction, the third consecutive clean draft.

procedure_signature.notes: Batch 4E skill 1/6 — opens the contact/friction inversion-retirement chain. Scope per Architect Batch 4E ruling: contact-force modeling only. All four ruled hard stops verified absent from every step by Operator — no friction-law selection, no mu*N calculation, no static/kinetic/impending regime decision, no equilibrium solving. Duplicate hazard against the signed support_reaction_modeling (a3e5cba6) cleared at the review beat; the two share the CONTACT_AND_SUPPORTS subtopic. That skill maps IDEALIZED support types to reaction components, and its frictionless roller idealizes contact away to a single force perpendicular to the surface with no tangent component by assumption. This skill models a REAL interface, where a normal acts perpendicular to the surface and a tangent force MAY exist along it — the tangent force is exactly what the frictionless idealization deletes, and it is this skill's distinctive content. Worked example: uniform bar AB, lower end A on a ROUGH plane inclined at 30 degrees, upper end B against a SMOOTH vertical wall; on the bar, N_A perpendicular to the incline (tilted 30 degrees from vertical) as a push plus f_A along the incline because A is rough, and N_B horizontal as a push with NO tangent because B is frictionless. Qualitative deliverable, magnitudes unknown — correct for a modeling skill, matching the support_reaction_modeling precedent. 2-signal mapping per the Architect's pre-ruling, content-earned: sign_or_placement_error at step 3 (where the contact forces are placed relative to the surface), unclassified at step 6 (the verify-and-stop step). axis_confusion correctly OMITTED: no authored step resolves a force into components. An inclined surface does not by itself earn the signal — ORIENTING a normal perpendicular to a surface is placement, not resolution, and placement is sign_or_placement_error's territory. Precedent: the signal attaches to genuine resolution steps (friction_equilibrium_sliding step 5, rigid_body_equilibrium_2d step 3). simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. Review-beat correction: the original example had a single ROUGH interface, so the tangent force was drawn mechanically and the applicability decision the Architect's scope names — 'place possible friction/contact tangent force along the surface WHEN APPLICABLE' — was never made. A student believing friction exists at every contact would have scored the example fully correct, which is the precise misconception this skill exists to separate from the frictionless idealization. A second, SMOOTH interface was added so the decision is live at B. Same defect family as the symmetric worked example on general_distributed_load_resultant and the inclined force placed at the moment centre on rigid_body_equilibrium_2d: the example must punish the error the signal names. formula.variables correctly declares only N_A, f_A, N_B, and theta — mu_s, mu_k, and the equilibrium sigma symbols appear in the file only where they name the ruled-out boundary, and declaring them would imply this skill uses them.

procedure_signature.notes: Three-dimensional rigid-body free-body diagram as an inventory of transmitted reaction components. First novel_lane 3D skill of Batch 4L. Support models independently checked against standard practice: a ball-and-socket prevents three translations and permits three rotations, so it transmits three force components and no couple moment, contributing three unknowns; a single cable of known direction transmits one tension along its line of action and cannot push, contributing one; a properly aligned journal bearing with its shaft along x, with the body supported elsewhere, transmits two force components perpendicular to the shaft and no couple moment, contributing two. Total six unknown reaction components. The properly-aligned modelling assumption is stated explicitly, and the poorly-aligned or sole-support case that would additionally carry two couple-moment components is named as not exercised. DISTINGUISHING FEATURE verified to bite rather than be asserted: the fixed-support contrast shows the same lettered support at A rising from three unknowns to six — A_x, A_y, A_z plus M_Ax, M_Ay, M_Az — purely because it prevents rotations as well as translations, which is precisely the inventory error that carrying a 2D pin habit into 3D produces. VERIFICATION FRAMING, the item of greatest review concern and correctly handled: the completeness count of six unknowns against the six independent 3D equilibrium equations is the exact coincidence that invites an unwarranted determinacy claim, and the artifact refuses it in both the procedure step and the solution step, naming all-parallel and common-line reaction configurations as cases where six unknowns still leaves a body improperly constrained, and assigning determinacy and improper-constraint analysis to constraints_static_determinacy and improper_constraint_detection. Honest limitation recorded: the count tests enumeration, not physical correctness of each support model — a misclassification preserving the total unknown count would pass undetected, while one changing the total would be caught. BOUNDARY: rigid_body_fbd_2d, signed in the SAME subtopic, owns the planar case and is extended here without the isolation principle being re-derived; particle_fbd_3d, signed, owns the concurrent-force particle case and is contrasted in one sentence, since distributed points of application are what admit couple-moment reactions; cross_product_moment_3d owns moment computation and none is performed. Verified that no equilibrium equation is written or solved, no moment is computed, and no numeric reaction value is reported anywhere. SYMBOL CONTINUITY, deliberate: A_x, A_y, A_z and applied P continue the naming convention of the signed 2D sibling into three dimensions, with M_Ax, M_Ay, M_Az and M_app as the intended 3D extension — continuity of meaning rather than collision. No binding of r, F, M_O, Fx, Fy, Fz, i, j, k, u, theta or d, all owned by signed skills. Two earned signals: sign_or_placement_error at step 4 where the support-reaction rule is applied and components are assigned, and unclassified at step 1 per Architect ruling MAPPING_DEFECT / NOT_NEW_SIGNAL as the earliest general recovery step. axis_confusion omitted as unearned, argued rather than inherited: no authored step performs resolution or measures an axis distance, and misjudging which components a support transmits is a support-model error rather than an axis error — the same disposition both signed FBD siblings reached, but reasoned independently here. simple_average_used forbidden, no averaging step; solution_sequencing_error omitted, supports being inventoried independently with no stranded prerequisite. SCHEMA-FIT FINDING, second data point for the Architect ruling on conceptual skills: formula.notation strained in the same class as scalar_vector_classification. This is an inventory skill with no algebra, so the field holds the support-reaction rule in prose — one force component per prevented translation, one couple-moment component per prevented rotation — and the declared variables are component names appearing in the inventory rather than symbols in an equation. No algebra was invented to fill the field. OPERATOR NOTE, non-blocking: the unclassified trigger includes omission of the properly-aligned bearing assumption while targeting step 1, though that assumption is authored at step 4 — one clause in an otherwise correctly placed general fallback, logged with the batch mapping-granularity notes rather than corrected in lane.

procedure_signature.notes: Batch 4D skill 1/3 — opens the rigid-body/support-reaction spine. Scope per Architect Batch 4D ruling: support-type to reaction-component mapping only; every step verified by Operator to stop before equilibrium equations and before solving for reactions (those are skills 2/3 and 3/3). Boundary against the already-signed rigid_body_fbd_2d (325894c7) verified at the review beat: that skill touches pin and roller INCIDENTALLY to complete one body's inventory; this one is the SYSTEMATIC catalog and covers the fixed support's couple-moment reaction MA and the two-force link F_CD, neither of which appears in rigid_body_fbd_2d. A couple appears there only as an applied load, never as a support reaction. Concept leads with the generative rule — the reactions a support exerts are exactly the motions it prevents — rather than a memorized table. 2-signal mapping per the Architect's pre-ruling: sign_or_placement_error at step 3 (the constraint-to-reaction mapping step), unclassified at step 7 (scope-boundary confirmation). axis_confusion correctly absent: the scope contains no component-resolution step, so no step can earn it. simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. Review-beat corrections: sign_or_placement_error retargeted 5 -> 3 because three of its four trigger clauses are mapping errors decided at step 3, while step 5 only transcribes the mapping onto the FBD (same retarget precedent as rigid_body_fbd_2d, 5 -> 4); formula.variables reduced to the five real symbols after declaring support TYPES as symbols and a combined 'Ax, Ay' entry; the worked example's count check now records that 5 reaction unknowns against 3 equilibrium equations makes the body statically indeterminate and that determinacy is not assessed in this skill — a fixed support alone exhausts all three 2D equilibrium equations, so any single body exercising fixed + roller + link is necessarily indeterminate, which is correct for a modeling-only scope but must not be left implying solvability.
